claim: mobjinfo[NUMMOBJTYPES] OOB read flagged after the doomednum-match loop (p_mobj.c:623,767)
rationale: Both sites are guarded by 'if (i==NUMMOBJTYPES) I_Error(...)' immediately before the mobjinfo[i] access; I_Error ends in exit(-1) (noreturn). cppcheck does not model the C11 _Noreturn keyword on the i_system.h prototype, so it assumes I_Error returns and reports a phantom OOB. Code is correct.

topic: | ammo >= NUMAMMO) I_Error(...)' (DOOM-0021 fixed the >NUMAMMO off-by-one to >=). I_Error is noreturn (exit -1) but cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn, so it cannot see the guard short-circuits the access. cppcheck's own 'condition redundant OR index accessed' wording confirms the guard. Code is correct.|cppcheck-noreturn-not-modeled

rationale: music is set in the if/else at 657-663: the bad-number branch calls I_Error (exit -1, _Noreturn), the else assigns &S_music[musicnum]. So music is always initialised at line 665. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn, so it cannot see the I_Error branch never falls through. Same blind spot as p_mobj/p_inter. Code is correct.

leftvol is clamped at 341-342: 'if (leftvol < 0 || leftvol > 127) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn, so leftvol is in [0,127] at line 346 and vol_lookup[leftvol*256] is in range. cppcheck cannot model the noreturn guard. Code is correct.

actor->target is null-checked at 375-376: 'if (!actor->target) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn, so actor->target is non-null when dereferenced at 381-382. cppcheck cannot model the noreturn guard. Code is correct.

momz is fixed_t (signed). The arithmetic right shift of a negative value is the intended fixed-point divide-toward-negative-infinity for the landing squat. On every platform DOOM targets (two's complement, gcc) >> on a negative int is an arithmetic shift. Replacing with /8 would change rounding (toward zero) and alter the squat feel. Intentional original DOOM behaviour - do not touch.

ANG90 is 0x40000000 (angle_t). The expression 'angle - player->mo->angle' is deliberate unsigned angle_t wrap arithmetic compared against signed -ANG90/20; the values do not actually overflow at runtime (-0x40000000/20 = -53687091, well within int). This is load-bearing original DOOM angle math used identically in every port. Touching it would break the chainsaw turn-to-face. Intentional - do not touch.

The range check at 433-436 is under '#ifdef RANGECHECK'. In release builds texturecolumn is kept in range by the upstream vis->x1/x2 clamping in R_ProjectSprite, exactly as in vanilla DOOM and Chocolate Doom. Adding an unconditional clamp here would change renderer behaviour (skip columns vanilla would draw). Project goal is to keep original DOOM rendering. Leave as-is.

min_x/max_x are seeded with MAXINT/-MAXINT then narrowed to real vertex coordinates by the loop at 398-409. A loaded map always has vertices, and map coords are bounded far below MAXINT, so the subtraction never underflows in practice. cppcheck assumes the worst-case seed range. Theoretical only; vanilla code. Leave as-is.
